thread:
Alex: Heads-up: post-RFC we need to lock down automated-exit criteria and clarify which decisions live in control-plane vs runtime. Goals: tiny blast radius, measurable SLA delta, cheap runtime checks. Ideas?
Mira: my vote: push policy evaluation to control-plane. Runtime should only do cheap probes and a catastrophic short-circuit path. Keep runtime surface minimal.
Sam: worry: control-plane is too slow for sudden QoS spikes (user impact in <30s). We need something local for speed.
Jordan: hybrid model works: runtime runs low-latency detectors for severe patterns (e.g., sustained 5xx spike) and emits a candidate rollback event to control-plane for confirmation/coordination.
Priya: telemetry we need: per-route qps, P50/P95/P99, 5xx rate, client error breakdown, and sampled output-quality flags. Suggest 60s aggregation windows with a rolling 5m baseline for delta comparisons.
Alex: draft exit conditions for auto-action: (1) error_rate > 2% over 2m AND >2x baseline, OR (2) P95 latency +300ms AND >1.5x baseline. Manual overrides always allowed.
Sam: add anti-flap: require 3 consecutive violating windows before an automated rollback triggers.
Mira: also add a throttled-degrade path: for mild regressions step-down canary traffic (e.g., -20%) instead of full rollback, then monitor closely.
Jordan: runtime <-> control-plane interface idea: control-plane exposes /v1/fallbacks; runtime subscribes via SSE or short poll. Example payload: `{"variant":"canary-2025-03","action":"reduce","pct":20,"expires_at":1758506000}`
Jordan: runtime short-circuit must be idempotent and emit deterministic reason codes like `short_circuit:error_spike` for audit/replay.
Priya: quality signals: sampled human eval stream and lightweight model-check heuristics (toxicity, repetition, hallucination proxies). For quality-triggered rollbacks, require both signal and a small-sample human check if ambiguous.
sre-bot: Incident policy updated: when auto-rollback occurs post here to #oncall, grab traces and snapshot dash links https://runbooks/relaunch :rotating_light:
Alex: operational flow: (a) runtime detector flags candidate, (b) control-plane evaluates policy, (c) control-plane issues `reduce` or `rollback` action, (d) runtime applies and ack's. For catastrophic detections runtime may `short_circuit` immediately then report.
Sam: test plan: unit tests for short-circuit idempotency, e2e for control-plane decision loop with injected metric regressions, chaos-run to validate no split-brain.
Mira: make sure to record provenance: why action happened, metric deltas, and who/what authorized it. Audit log format suggestion: `timestamp,actor,variant,action,reason_code,metrics_snapshot` (keep as stringified map).
Alex: follow-ups: Sam writes specific RFC enumerating metric names, window sizes, exact thresholds, and API schema. Runtime implements short-circuit tests + SSE client. SRE wires alerts -> playbook. 30m sync tomorrow with SRE+runtime.
Priya: add small-sample human-in-loop step for non-obvious quality failures; keep it gated so we don't block latency/error-driven rollbacks.
Mira: agreed. We'll bifurcate the automation: fast path (latency/errors) and conservative path (quality-required).
Alex: cool. I'll capture notes in RFC template and link existing dashboards in the draft. Thanks all!
